dedupe_keys.name: doe commercial reference buildings 16 building types energyplus

description: The DOE commercial reference buildings, formerly called commercial building benchmark models, were developed by the U.S. Department of Energy with three national laboratories to give complete descriptions for whole-building energy analysis in EnergyPlus and a consistent baseline for comparing simulations. Sixteen building types, from large, medium and small offices, warehouses, retail, schools, supermarkets and restaurants to hospitals, outpatient clinics, hotels and midrise apartments, represent about 70% of U.S. commercial buildings, with floor areas and storey counts listed for each; they are modelled in 16 locations covering all U.S. climate zones, starting from Miami in zone 1A. Versions exist for new construction, existing buildings built in or after 1980 and existing buildings built before 1980, and a report from the National Laboratory of the Rockies describes them as models of the national building stock. Coverage: U.S. climate zones. Access: free downloads from the DOE page, last updated in April 2026. Licence: U.S. government work. Caveats: the models are older than the current prototype suite and not tied to recent code editions. Simulation uses are archetypes of existing and new commercial buildings for stock energy, retrofit and hazard impact studies. Related records: the DOE/PNNL prototype building models and EnergyPlus.
